symptom: on a Mendix 9.24 project MDL-WORKFLOW10 suggested `change $T (System.WorkflowUserTask_Assignees = …)`; check --references accepted it and the build failed CE1613, while the name 9.24 actually has (WorkflowUserTask_Assignee) was refused by exec as 'not a known association'
cause: modelsdk/meta's System module described the 11.x platform for every project; check never resolved a one-dot `Module.Assoc` member at all (only that Module is a module), so check and exec disagreed
file: modelsdk/meta/system_module.go (SystemAssocDef.Introduced/Removed, ModelerSystemAssociationsIn), mdl/backend/modelsdk/system_module_read.go (version-aware System model), mdl/executor/validate_task_claim.go, mdl/executor/validate_member_refs.go (moduleLacksAssociation)
insight: The System module is not in the .mpr, so version facts about it must be measured from the platform itself: the modeler assembly embeds the System domain model as BSON, so grep it per version (mxcli setup mxbuild --version <exact build>; the CDN listing in the error gives build numbers) and read Name/Type/GUID around the hit. Assignee (9.24, Reference) and Assignees (10.0+, ReferenceSet) share GUID and ParentPointer — a rename, not a new member. Record only measured differences as Introduced/Removed and keep the version-blind list = current platform, so existing callers are unchanged. Disk: each extracted mxbuild is ~1-2 GB; clear old app copies first.
